relevance_note: Cohort of 31 suspected Behcet's disease patients in which 'Five patients (cases 5, 10, 14, 29, 31) were classified as having Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20)', each with individual-level clinical and variant data in Table 1.
method_note: Read the whole Markdown (main text, Table 1, Supplementary Tables S1-S4 and figure legends) and wrote all rows by hand in a short Python script that only assembles the JSON and checks spans; no script transcribed a table. Scope: 31-patient Behcet's disease cohort; only the five HA20 cases (5, 10, 14, 29, 31) have TNFAIP3 variants. In-scope relatives: mother of Case 10 ('Similar features in mother'), mother of Case 14 (autoimmune hypothyroidism), and the mother, maternal grandmother and brother of Case 29. The 'maternal cousins' of Case 29 got no rows because their number is not stated. The supplementary text says the mother of Case 29 harboured the mutation; Table 1 says the variant was found in the mother 'but not other mildly affected relatives' - it is unclear whether the grandmother and brother were tested negative or not tested, so no variant rows for them. Labels: Table 1 'Case' column holds bare numbers but the text uses 'case 5', 'Case 29' etc., so labels are 'Case <n>'. Ages are Table 1 'Age' = age at the time of this study (recorded as last evaluation; unit years assumed from the cohort median '15 years'). is_proband left null for cases: the paper does not call them probands. Contradictions/discrepancies: (1) Table 1 lists two TNFAIP3 variants for Case 10 (946G>A G316S and 1625_1626insGAC TACAGCAGAGGCC S548Dfs*128), while the abstract, results and discussion list only S548Dfs*128 for the five cases; both table rows were recorded. (2) Table 1 'Variant classification' is 3 for every TNFAIP3 variant (Methods: Class 3 = unknown significance), while the Discussion says six of the seven novel disease-causing variants 'can be classified as pathogenic' and only case 5's p.T76I remains a VUS; pathogenicity was taken from each person's own row (class 3), with case 5 as VUS. (3) Results say the NF-kB assay 'showed upregulation of the pathway in all four cases' (5, 14, 29, 31) but Supplementary Fig. S1 legend says case 29 'showed less activation' (attributed to treatment); both quoted for case 29. (4) Case 14: Table 1 says 'chronic pulmonary interstitial emphysema', text says 'chronic interstitial pneumonia'; both recorded as observed. Variant type not recorded (paper states no class for these variants). Transcript not printed (only 'HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee RefSeq transcript'). Table note a ('Family DNA was available ... segregation analysis') applies to cases 5 and 14 but does not mention parents, so parental_testing_statement left 'not reported' for them. Case 10 'was unavailable for follow-up testing' (no functional data). Checklist judgments: 'redness of the eyes' (Case 5) not taken as ocular inflammation; perianal ulcers (Cases 29, 31) not counted as GI ulcers (Case 29 GI item observed via colitis); tonsilitis not counted as recurrent infection; headaches not counted as CNS involvement; autoimmune hypothyroidism counted as autoimmune thyroiditis; livedo reticularis (Case 29) counted under skin lesions. No features were explicitly excluded for any in-scope person; no stacked ' / ' cells occur.
